summary: Three generated functions are SECURITY DEFINER (_delta_holders, _delta_serial_new, _delta_serial_past), so their generated predicates are the only guard there
detail: Any compiler bug in a permission check is a data leak, as October showed. The handover's direction for delta: run compiled functions as the invoker under FORCE RLS so row-level security is the backstop. Decide whether dzql adopts that or the path compiler moves to delta.
note: 2026-10-16: the path compiler moved to delta (owns as a path, compiled per document, a row never handed away). Derived RLS is still to do: probed, PGlite enforces RLS for a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role, so it can be tested without a server; but the fan-out (holders, told) reads other documents' rows inside the writer's transaction, so invoker functions under FORCE RLS need policies that let it, or the fan-out runs as the owner. Its own piece of work.; 2026-10-20: fixed: generateSql derives row-level security from the paths (compilePolicies: dzql_may__<collection>, the policy dzql_owns, enabled and forced by 001b's _delta_govern) on each table every document holding it says by a path; the compiled reads and writes run as the invoker beneath it. The fan-out stays a narrow SECURITY DEFINER (_delta_holders answers names, never rows; _delta_told works as the writer on the write's own rows), with dzql_owns__ and the policies' lookups: a policy that let the writer read other documents' rows for the fan-out would let it read them anywhere. Definers raise dzql.definer, which a policy lets past for the table's owner alone, so FORCE holds a single role that owns its tables too. Proved on PGlite as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role: tests/delta-pg/rls-backstop-pglite.test.ts (an owns, a scope and an open made wrong on purpose leak as the superuser and are refused as the role; the fan-out reaching a board the writer cannot read; the owner's export and migrate), tests/compile/policies.test.ts, and delta's permission cases as the role

summary: A schema per app on one database is not supported: the change channel is database-wide
detail: With the framework retired (todo #26), one generateSql serves one app's definitions, so two apps on one Postgres server each need a database of their own (CREATE DATABASE; LISTEN/NOTIFY is per database). Peter asked (2026-10-16) whether Postgres schemas could separate apps within one database instead: lighter to administer. They could: each app's _delta_* tables, ledger, dispatchers and compiled functions live in its schema, and the SECURITY DEFINER functions already pin the search path they were applied with. Missing: the pool's search_path set to the app's schema (applyFramework, applySql, createDocListener), and NOTIFY on a channel named for the schema (delta_changes is database-wide, so each app would hear the other's names; harmless to the subscribers, but a custom document reads each one). Wants a test with two apps in two schemas of one database, each writing, undoing and told only its own.
note: 2026-10-20: fixed: namespace on openStore, openDatabase, applyFramework, applySql and createDocListener keeps an app in a Postgres schema of its own, made when missing; 001c tells its changes on _delta_channel() (delta:<schema>; public keeps delta_changes) and keys a listener's lock by the schema; PGlite gives each query its pool's path. tests/delta-pg/namespaces.test.ts: two apps of one table and document name, on one PGlite and on the server through openStore, each writing, undoing and told only its own; docs/postgres/postgres.md, Several apps on one database

summary: A harness test timed out once (30 s) in the fast tier, and every later test in the file failed after it
detail: 'a write that is not on the ledger fails, unless its resource keeps it off' timed out in a bun run affected on 19 October (dzql's tier took 51 s, its usual is 27), and the 17 tests after it in harness.test.ts failed with it: they share the run it left. It passed alone, in the rerun, and in four gate runs that day. Since that morning the harness opens the app's SQLite when a run asks (a dynamic import in sqliteStore), not as it loads: look there first if it comes back. Kin to #55 and #56, which also fail only under a busy machine.
note: 2026-10-19: seen once; not reproduced; 2026-10-20: not seen again: a dozen gate runs and fast tiers today, dzql's tier once at 69 s under load, and harness.test.ts passed every time. Closed; raise again if it recurs; 2026-10-20 (later): seen again, so reopened: in an agent's worktree, dzql's test:fast had a stories-harness test time out at 30 s and the rest of harness.test.ts fail with 'cannot start a transaction within a transaction' (the story store's BEGIN left open by the timed-out test); it passed on a clean rerun and inside affected. The cause to look at: a timed-out test leaves sqliteStore's transaction open, so every later test in the file fails with it. The fix is the store's end() in a finally, or begin() rolling back what a test left; 2026-10-20: fixed, the cascade: the story store's begin() rolls back a transaction a timed-out story left open, so a timeout costs its own test, never the file's other tests (harness.test.ts holds it; it fails with the guard taken out). Whether a story can still take 30 s on a loaded Mac is a timing question, not this: raise it again only if a single test times out

summary: A ref to a row a story removes must still show what it named: the cafe's orders copied the dish's name and price instead of naming the dish
detail: Decided (#52): an order names its dish (dish: menu:/items) and says ordered_at, and reads the dish and its price as they stood then, rather than copying them. A page is drawn synchronously from the documents the kernel holds (src/rendering/documents.ts), and a dish taken off the menu is a closed version no held document has; open_at is a call, not a held read. The seam: the kernel holds a ref's rows as they stood (a document of the referenced collection's versions, or open_at held per time), read as any document is. Then the cafe's model changes (orders: dish, ordered_at; a migration), its table resource writes the ref, and the floor and the table read the dish through it.
note: 2026-10-20: split from #52 when the examples' history landed; 2026-10-20: fixed, by Peter's design (genoa's surrogate, the label that stands in for a key): an order keeps the key (dish, dish_id) and its surrogate beside it, the dish's name and price copied as it is ordered (dish_name, dish_price); while the dish is on the menu it shows the menu's, once taken off its own copy (orderOf). No kernel seam needed: the page holds the menu, which whoever holds the orders holds. The model's check advises a surrogate (ref-surrogate) on a ref whose row a story removes, in place of a time (undated-ref, gone); migration 002 renames item and price to the surrogate, so no order loses what it said; model story 14 (the manager cannot change the menu), since the manager now holds it; the read-back compares a ref by its column

summary: A client-named id of 2^53-1 moves a table's serial there, and every id minted after it is refused for good
detail: _delta_serial_past accepts p_id = 9007199254740991 (it returns only for p_id > it), setval moves the sequence there, and the next add mints 2^53, which _delta_row_id refuses (past 2^53 - 1): that table's new rows can never be replaced or removed. Probe: add /courses/9007199254740991, then add /courses/-, then remove it: refused. Anyone permitted an add with a client-chosen id can do it. Fix: _delta_serial_past moves the serial only up to a bound below 2^53-1 (refuse a client id that would leave no room), and _delta_next_id raises before 2^53. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: a named id moves the serial at most to 2^53-1 less 2^32 (_delta_serial_past), so the table can always mint an id it can name; a mint past 2^53-1 is refused (2200H, _delta_next_id). delta's shared case keeps add /courses/9007199254740991, so such an id is not refused as the item proposed. tests/compile/serial.test.ts.

summary: signInLinks are permanent bearer tokens: reusable, never expiring, printed to stdout, listed to anonymous visitors in the cafe
detail: The tokens live in process memory for the life of the process (links.ts:21), are reusable, sit in the URL path (proxy and access logs record them), are printed at start (cafe routes.ts:58, on Railway that is the logs), and the cafe's home page lists every person's link to anyone. Each instance mints its own, so two replicas break them, and GET /in/:token is a login CSRF. delta's auth-link already does it properly (single use, expiring, hashed). Fix: in production (NODE_ENV=production) never print or list the links; make them single use with an expiry; say plainly in signin.md that signInLinks is a demo door, and how a production app signs people in. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: signInLinks is a demo door: each link used once, running out (ttl, 15 min), kept as its token's hash; opened it only asks, a page whose form posts it, refused from another Origin (the login CSRF); under NODE_ENV=production none is said, listed or opened (say() gives DEMO_DOOR); the cafe lists staff only in development; signin.md says what production uses. Links are still per-process memory: fine for a door shut in production.

summary: Undo and redo skip sees and permit: the cafe's customer can un-pay an invoice
detail: walk (server.ts:332-358) writes to whatever document the cursor names; without permitUndo it is allowed by design (resource.ts:83-91), and a document the session no longer sees can still be walked. The cafe customer may only set paid=true (table-api.ts:40), but Undo puts it back. Fix: re-check sees on the walk's document, default permitUndo to permit over the inverse ops, and mark the cafe's pay undoable:false. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: in part: Resource.undoable may be a function of each shaped write; the cafe's paying is never undone, and its table's permitUndo refuses an undo or redo changing a paid invoice (story annCannotTakeBack). Not made, measured: defaulting permitUndo to permit over the walk's ops refused 31 stories across the five examples (permit judges what a page sends, before shape and with rows as "-"; "Undo may do what permit refuses" is the documented contract), and re-checking sees on the walk's document refused the cafe manager's undo of "placed". For Peter: which contract undo keeps. The model's guards never see walks either (guardWrites hooks only delta).

summary: Sessions never expire, and a row is made for every new cookie
detail: The session cookie has no Max-Age and the server never expires a session (server.ts:36-38), so a stolen cookie works forever; sessionRows.of makes a row for every new cookie (sessions.ts:80-94), so bots opening sockets fill the table. Fix: an expiry, renewed on use, and idle anonymous rows collected. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: the cookie has Max-Age (Example.sessionDays, 30), set again on every socket; sessionRows(..., { seen, days, expired }) keeps the last use (renewed at most daily), names a fresh session past its days, and lets expired rows go at most hourly through the app's expired: document; the cafe opts in. The server check is opt-in, since it needs the column.

summary: Every open re-applies the framework and compiled SQL, a file per transaction: a starting instance breaks every running one
detail: app-store.ts:250-251 runs applyFramework then applySql(generateSql(...)) on every open, changed or not; applyFramework commits each 001* file on its own (bootstrap.ts:71-75), putting back the uncompiled stubs ("no doc def") until generateSql commits, and the DDL takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks even when nothing changes. Measured: about 100 of 280 concurrent writes failed while a second store opened; behind one open reporting transaction the start queued and stalled plain reads. Fix: apply framework and compiled SQL in one transaction, keep a hash of it in the database and skip the DDL when it matches, with a lock_timeout. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: openStore applies the framework and the compiled SQL in one transaction (applyCompiled, bootstrap.ts) with lock_timeout 5 s and 3 tries; _delta_compiled keeps the set's hash, and an open of an unchanged app runs no DDL; postgres-open-skew.test.ts: every write made during a second open succeeds (on HEAD they failed).

summary: Whichever instance started last decides the documents for all: an old one restarting during a deploy undoes the new
detail: Starting a v2 store with four documents, then restarting a v1 store with one, made v2's write to boards: fail with 500 "no doc def for: boards:". postgres.md says two versions on one database each see their own; that holds for columns only. Fix: keep the compiled set's hash and a version with it, and refuse to replace a newer set with an older one. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: each compiled set gets a generation; a set a newer one has replaced is never applied again (the older server runs on the newer set and logs both); rollback: true or DZQL_ROLLBACK=1 puts it back as the newest; tested v2 opens, v1 restarts, v2's documents still work; postgres.md, Deploying.

summary: A ledger write opens the whole document to build its inverse: its cost grows with the document
detail: delta_apply_logged (001g:181-182) reads _delta_open(p_doc_name, TRUE) on every write, under the document's advisory lock; openStore turns the ledger on by default. One field replace on a document of N posts: 18 ms at 1k, 81 ms at 10k, 1,096 ms at 100k (3.7 and 8.6 ms without the ledger). The bench never times delta_apply_logged. Fix: build the inverse from the rows the write touches. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: _delta_apply(..., p_before) keeps each touched row as it was before its first touch (in scope, plus the cascade rows _delta_beside added); the inverse is taken from those. 10k rows 149 -> 3.8 ms, 100k 1,523 -> 3.9 ms. tests/compile/inverse.test.ts holds it to the old inverse over 31 kinds of write.

summary: One app-wide event queue, a whole redraw per reader and a quadratic parts layout: a busy document stalls everyone
detail: server.ts:251-257 puts every socket's events through one queue waiting on the global quiet(); every page that read a document is redrawn whole (server.ts:176); layout compares every part with every other through includes (parts.ts:188-203). Layout alone: 50 rows 2 ms per change, 500 rows 72 ms, 1,000 rows 305 ms. Chat, 200 clients in one room: 50 messages reached all in 33-42 s; a new tab waited 13.5 s behind queued writes. Fix: a linear layout from offsets recorded as part() is called; queue per socket; draw a socket at most once per change gathered; CPU per write in bun run costs. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: parts laid out from offsets read off the page once (the every-pair layout kept as the fallback and as what parts.test.ts holds it to); list diff by sets; each connection's events in a queue of its own; a page drawn once for all changes told while it waited. Chat, 200 in a room, 50 messages: 24.7 s -> 3.7 s; 1,000-row layout 200 ms -> 6 ms. CPU per write not in costs: costs checks sizes to 3%, and CPU swings with the machine.

summary: Backpressure is ignored: Bun drops messages to a slow socket and the page stays wrong
detail: send discards ws.send's status (server.ts:25); SOCKET sets no backpressureLimit (Bun's 16 MB) nor closeOnBackpressureLimit; sent.set runs before the send. Measured with the same options: of 600 sends of 60 KB to a reader that stopped, 252 were dropped and the socket stayed open. The client skips a fragment whose target is missing (app.ts:527-529) and never checks versions for a gap. Fix: close a socket past a small backpressure limit (it reconnects and is drawn afresh) or mark it behind on a failed send; the client asks for the page whole when a target is missing. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: SOCKET closes a socket once 1 MiB waits for it (backpressureLimit, closeOnBackpressureLimit; tests/rendering/load.test.ts); the client asks for the page whole on a part whose target it lacks, or a patch past the next version a watching applet holds. WIRE 5.

summary: Nothing limits what one connection sends: one user can stall the app
detail: enqueue has no limit; a message that is not a write is answered with the whole page (server.ts:419); a write may carry unbounded ops up to 1 MiB, and each test op re-parses the whole last page (server.ts:377, parts.ts:300): about 21k test ops at 1 ms each block every user for about 20 s. Fix: cap ops per write, parse the page once per write, cap the events a socket may have queued (closing past it). (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: a write of more than MOST_OPS (1,000) ops is refused (TOO_MANY_OPS); drawnFields reads the page once for all of a write's tests; a connection with more than MOST_WAITING (100) events waiting is closed (1008).

summary: The starter quietly deploys PGlite, which dzql's own docs forbid
detail: docs/postgres/postgres.md:168 says never deploy PGlite; the template's store.ts and CLAUDE.md present PGlite in the data folder, "a Railway volume", and bun start with no DATABASE_URL runs PGlite with no warning. Fix: under NODE_ENV=production refuse to start without DATABASE_URL; take "a Railway volume" out of the PGlite wording. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: openStore's part: under NODE_ENV=production with no server named it refuses PGlite with an error naming DATABASE_URL, unless pgliteInProduction: true or DZQL_PGLITE_IN_PRODUCTION=1 (deploy.md names both). With the template's wording, done.

summary: There is no deployment story: no Dockerfile, no hosting page, nothing on TLS, the pool, poolers or a proxy
detail: No Dockerfile, Procfile or hosting guide for a dzql app; nothing on sslmode, the pool's size, that LISTEN rules out transaction-mode poolers (PgBouncer, Supabase/Neon pooled URLs), ETA_ORIGINS behind a proxy, backups (pg_dump; exportTables is not a backup), or what to watch. Fix: a Dockerfile in the template and a deploy reference page in the dzql-app skill: the environment, TLS, the pooler rule, the proxy, backups, the role (not a superuser). (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: template/Dockerfile (oven/bun:1.4.3-slim, bun install --production --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts, NODE_ENV=production, PID_FILE=/tmp/server.pid, USER bun, bun start) and template/dockerignore (dotted by cli.ts, as gitignore is); reference/deploy.md, linked from SKILL.md's step 9; create-dzql's test holds the FROM to packageManager. The image is built by no test (no Docker where it was made).

summary: An exclusion, check or raised refusal from the database answers 500
detail: CODE_OF_SQLSTATE (listener.ts:109) has no 23P01 (exclusion_violation), 23514 (check_violation) or P0001 (raise_exception), so a constraint an app adds for double-booking, a balanced entry or a closed period reaches the writer as the server's failure. Fix: 23P01 409, 23514 400, P0001 400. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: 23514 and P0001 answer 400, 23P01 409; tested with a CHECK, an EXCLUDE and a trigger RAISE added in a migration (app-store-answers-pglite.test.ts).

summary: _delta_ops_log is never pruned unless the app calls pruneOpsLog, which nothing does
detail: Each write adds a row per document it tells; pruneOpsLog exists (postgres/schema.ts:37) but openStore, the listener, the template and the examples never call it, and the table has no index for pruning by age. Fix: the store prunes on an interval under an advisory lock; an index for it; the ledger's and histories' retention documented. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: the index part: idx_delta_ops_log_created on _delta_ops_log(created_at), so delta_prune_ops's delete by age uses it (indexes.test.ts). The timed pruning is the Postgres runtime's stream. 2026-10-22: pruning: an open store prunes the ops log (every 10 min, keep 1 hour) under a try-advisory-lock per schema, stopped on close; prune: false opts out; retention in postgres.md, Deploying. With the index, done.

summary: Columns the documents look up by get no index: refs, scopes, owns paths
detail: Only parent keys and temporal (id, valid_to) are indexed. Measured on 1M rows: removing an unreferenced film 320 ms (a scan of showings, for the refs check); opening a scoped list 77-108 ms; each owns check 18 ms (a scan of members). Fix: derive an index for each column a refs, scope or owns path filters by. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: generateSql adds idx_<table>_<column> on (column, id) for each column a refs, cascadeOn, scope or owns-path hop filters by (not id, parent keys, a unique's first column, booleans, json, like/at scopes); indexes.test.ts drops each and shows the plan go back to every row. 1M rows: refs 228 -> 2 ms, scoped open 85 -> 2 ms, owns 130 -> 1 ms.

summary: Two documents holding each other's rows deadlock: 5.4% of concurrent writes, answered 409 and not retried
detail: _delta_tell bumps _delta_versions with the writer's document first, then the others; two writers adding posts through board:5 and posts: deadlocked on 217 of 4,000 writes, each waiting out deadlock_timeout. Fix: bump every document in one sorted order. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: _delta_tell bumps every told document's version in one order (by name, C collation), then logs and notifies, writer first (_delta_log_and_notify); tests/delta-pg/tell-order.test.ts deadlocks every time before, passes 3 of 3 after.

summary: The migration fence scans the whole ledger inside the migration's transaction, with no lock_timeout
detail: The fence UPDATE (migrate.ts:67-70) took 42 s over 1M undoable entries, holding the altered table's lock all the while; migrations set no lock_timeout. Fix: fence by a ledger id watermark (or a partial index), and a lock_timeout on migrations. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: the fence runs ahead of the migration's transaction (a short SHARE lock reads the ledger's last id, then batches of 10,000; _delta_fences keeps how far each app is fenced); migrations take lock_timeout with 3 tries.

summary: The pool has no error handler and cannot be configured
detail: openDatabase is new Pool({ connectionString }) (pglite.ts:170): terminating the backends crashed Bun with an uncaught error from an idle client; no max, ssl, statement timeout or a Pool of the app's own can be given to openStore. Fix: pool.on("error") logged; openStore takes a pg.PoolConfig (or a Pool). (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: openDatabase logs an idle connection's error instead of crashing; openStore takes pool: a PoolConfig or the app's own Pool, used as is and never ended.

summary: Transaction-mode poolers (PgBouncer, pooled URLs) cannot carry the listener
detail: LISTEN, the holder's session-level advisory lock, the migration locks and the session-level dzql.definer setting need a real session. Fix: say so (session mode or a direct URL), in the deploy page. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: deploy.md says LISTEN, the holder's session-level lock, the open and migration locks and dzql.definer need a real session: a direct URL or a session-mode pooler, never transaction mode. 2026-10-22: and postgres.md, Deploying, says the same.

summary: With any custom document registered, every instance re-reads the ops log for every notification
detail: hearCustom (listener.ts:403-419) runs FETCH_LOG for every notification whenever a custom document is defined (custom.size counts definitions, not open views), one after another per instance. Fix: skip when no custom view is open. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: the listener counts the custom documents its sockets hold or are opening, and reads the log for them only while the count is above zero (a socket let go by owns stays counted until it closes: read for nothing then, never missed).

summary: Nothing warns that a superuser or BYPASSRLS pool makes RLS inert, nor that a rendering app never uses it
detail: Railway and Supabase hand you a superuser by default; RLS holds only a pool that is neither. The kernel reads every document once as no one (documents.ts:116), so for dzql/rendering apps owns and RLS never apply: sees, permit and how documents are cut protect the data. Fix: warn at open when auth is set and the role bypasses RLS; say both plainly in rls.md and the skill. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: with auth on a server, openStore warns when the pool's role is a superuser or BYPASSRLS (PGlite skipped); rls.md's "Where it applies, and where it does not"; a bullet in dzql-app's documents.md.

summary: A 500's database error text reaches the client
detail: withDoc, the custom open and walk send errMsg(err) for 500s (listener.ts:578-581, 619), exposing table, constraint and type details. Fix: a generic message for 5xx; the detail is logged. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: every 5xx from withDoc, a custom open, shape or a walk answers "The server failed: what went wrong is in its log", the detail logged.

summary: Definer functions are executable by PUBLIC
detail: dzql_owns__*(name, person) and the other SECURITY DEFINER functions keep PUBLIC's EXECUTE. Fix: REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC on the definer functions an app role need not call directly, where that holds the cases. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: every SECURITY DEFINER function is called as the app role (nested from the invoker delta_apply and _delta_tell, from _delta_keeps_reach, registry.ts and the RLS policies), and Postgres checks EXECUTE on nested calls; app roles have no grant but PUBLIC's, so revoking it breaks every app with its own role. Needs a design: an explicit grant to the app role (a generateSql option or dzql grant <role>) and registry.ts asking ownership through a wrapper bound to app.user_id. For Peter.

summary: auth-jwt takes a one-character secret, and login and register have no limit
detail: A secret of "x" signs in; a missing one fails only at the first login; login and register (auth-jwt.ts:130-158) each cost a bcrypt at cost 12 in Postgres with no limit, so an unauthenticated flood exhausts the database. Fix: require at least 32 bytes, checked at construction; a per-email limit on failed logins. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: jwtAuth throws as it is made for a secret under 32 bytes, or none; maxFailedLogins (5) per email within lockout (60 s), then refused without a bcrypt, cleared by a right password, counted per process.

summary: delta's socket on Postgres: history's limit is unclamped and opens per socket are unbounded
detail: history passes msg.limit to SQL as given (listener.ts:741); each open of an arbitrary name inserts into _delta_held. Fix: clamp history (100) and cap a socket's open documents. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: history's limit is clamped to 1..100 (default 50); createDocListener's maxOpen (1000) refuses one more document per socket with 429; in-process callers are exempt.

summary: A page that reads more than 20 documents not yet held fails, and they load one at a time
detail: settled gives up after 20 tries (documents.ts:215-221), loading one document per try and redrawing the whole page each time. Fix: gather every missing document of a drawing and load them together; no cap below what a page can read. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: inside settled a read not held is nothing, recorded; every document recorded is loaded together and the run repeated; the bound is 1,000 rounds (MOST_ROUNDS), not 20 documents.

summary: A drawing that throws is only logged: the tab stays on Connecting, or goes stale
detail: server.ts:82: on first open the shell's "Connecting..." stays for good. Fix: tell the page its drawing failed (a status the client shows), and log it. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: a drawing that throws is logged and the page sent {type: "failed"}; the client says "This page could not be drawn just now." in its role=status region until the next render, a first drawing too. WIRE 5.

summary: Every tab reconnects at the same moment after a restart
detail: The delay starts at 1 s and doubles with no jitter (app.ts:7-8, 862-863), and every tab is closed 1012 at once. Fix: full jitter. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: the client reconnects after Math.random() * the wait, the wait still doubling to 10 s.

summary: Undo handles are dropped when a session's last socket closes, so a reconnect breaks undo
detail: server.ts:489: any reconnect, to the same instance too, answers "No change of yours is called...". Fix: keep a session's handles for a grace period after its last socket closes. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: a session's handles are kept five minutes after its last socket closes (HANDLES_KEPT).

summary: An app cannot report the kernel's failures anywhere but the console
detail: failed() writes to console.error and onFailure is not exported. Fix: export it (dzql/rendering/failed) so an app can send failures where it watches. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: dzql/rendering/failed is exported (onFailure); example.md says to send failures where the app is watched.

summary: Every change clones the whole held document
detail: structuredClone (documents.ts:71) on the serialised path: 1.8 ms at 1,000 messages, 26 ms at 10,000. Fix: clone only what the ops touch, or apply ops to a document no drawing keeps. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: a change copies only the containers on each op's path (once a change); the rest is shared, never changed in place.

summary: Where the cookie is the session, naming each recipient scans every socket
detail: wireName scans every open socket for each recipient (audience.ts:325): a change costs O(N^2). Fix: an index from session to its wire name. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: audience.ts counts open sockets by session (open and close keep it); wireName asks the count.

summary: Every path answers 200 with the shell, and the title never changes
detail: server.ts:440: monitors and crawlers see no 404; <title> is fixed. Fix: an app may say which paths it has (404 otherwise), and a page's title is drawn. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: in part: Example.screens(path): a path that is none of the app's screens is 404, the shell all the same; omitted, every path is 200 as before; the cafe says its own. The title is not drawn: the page arrives over the socket, so the client would have to take a drawn title, a wire change.

summary: inspect returns delta's ledger id, the cross-document serial handles were made to hide
detail: resources/index.ts:95. Fix: return the handle. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: inspect names a change of yours by its handle (change), never the ledger's id.

summary: ETA_ORIGINS is not normalised: a trailing slash or a path fails closed silently
detail: Unlike delta's allowedOrigins. Fix: normalise each to its origin. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: each ETA_ORIGINS entry is taken as its URL origin; one that is no origin is reported through failed() and lets nothing in.

summary: No security headers on the page
detail: No Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy on the shell. Fix: send them with the page. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: the shell is sent with frame-ancestors 'self', nosniff and Referrer-Policy same-origin; the bundle sits at an unguessable path (<at>/__shell/<uuid>) that the page's routes fetch over the server's own URL (once in production), since Bun serves an HTML bundle with its own headers.

summary: The migrations page is SQLite only, while the starter is Postgres
detail: It shows db.run and openTables; the starter migrates through openStore({ migrations }), Migration<PoolClient>. Fix: a Postgres migration worked, with its Working: line. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: migrations.md opens with Postgres: openStore({ migrations: { dir } }), a changes-only 001 and a 002 with changes plus up(client: PoolClient); its Working: names the cafe's model/migrations and tests/readme/migrations.test.ts, which runs the page's two files as written over PGlite.

summary: The manual stops short of what a production app needs: email, jobs, files, external calls, export
detail: Covered: owns, permit, scope, serverWrite, routes. Absent: sending email, a background or scheduled job, file storage (the wedding keeps pictures as SQLite blobs), calling an external API, search, CSV export. Fix: a short pattern page, even where it is a route plus serverWrite. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: reference/patterns.md: email (an outbox row from afterWrite, sent by a job), a scheduled job (a timer composed into serve with its close, store.owner, pruneOpsLog, a lock for several instances), files (Bun.s3, the key on the row), another service, search (a defineCustomDoc recompute), CSV export (a route checked as the session).

summary: The template's scripts run node_modules/dzql/src files that are not exported
detail: stories, cli, model:load and model:check run dzql's internals, against "the public API is exports". Fix: run them through the dzql bin. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: the dzql bin gains dzql stories, dzql cli, dzql model load and dzql model built (src/cli/app.ts); the template's scripts run through them; create-dzql's test checks no script names node_modules/.

summary: The .server.pid guard refuses to start in a container over a pid that is not ours
detail: In a container the pid file can survive a restart while its pid is reused (often 1). Fix: skip the guard under NODE_ENV=production. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: the template's routes.ts removes .server.pid before run() under NODE_ENV=production; create-dzql's start test writes a pid file naming a live process first (reverted, it fails "Already running").

summary: Every position write pays for versions, the ops log and telling: 250-400 writes a second per process
detail: Vehicle tracking needs more; memory documents are per process. For Peter: a fact write path, or a memory document fed over NOTIFY. (Production review, 22 October.)

summary: A row a trigger changes is never told to the documents holding it
detail: A trigger on lines keeping accounts.balance changed the row, but the open chart: was told nothing. Fix: delta_touch(collection, id), callable from a trigger, adds a row to the write's touched set. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: delta_touch(collection, id), from a trigger a write sets off, adds the row to that write's touched set (held for the transaction, saved and restored around nested writes); before the change the changed fields are told, after it every field; outside a write it does nothing. tests/delta-pg/touch-pglite.test.ts; docs/postgres/sql.md.

summary: leave's team:1 holds every request ever made, and clashes are only shown
detail: The window scope (a document named by a date range) is the fix, and an exclusion constraint would refuse a clash. Fix: leave shows both, once the database can refuse an overlap. (Production review, 22 October.)
note: 2026-10-22: in part: leave's starts/ends are date columns and the requests' noOverlap (person_id, "[]") refuses a request over days its person already holds, with a story. Left: the window scope, which needs a decision: the team resource's resolveDoc becoming team-in:<from>:<until> (then shape supplies teams_id, and a move outside the shown weeks is 404), or staying team:1 (told every request, which #124 wants gone).

summary: An undo or redo still reads its document whole
detail: _delta_walk_plan opens the document (_delta_open_held) to guard the walk, so a walk costs the document's size as a ledger write did before #88. Fix: guard from the rows the entry touched, as the write now does. (Found fixing #88, 22 October.)

summary: On one database kept between runs, the Postgres suite's files trip on each other
detail: Run on a DATABASE_URL that is not emptied first: app-store-pglite and app-store-owner-pglite fail after postgres-examples.test.ts, and auth-link (a person past 2^31) on a big-link row an earlier run left (app-store-signed-in-pglite after it). The same on HEAD before the review's changes; test:pg's fresh database hides it. Fix: each file cleans what it makes, or runs in a schema of its own. (Found 22 October.)

summary: The client half of the coverage gate is never judged: testFiles() counts an eval fixture no run loads
detail: testFiles() includes evals/fixtures/leave-page-on-session/**/*.test.ts, which scripts/tests.ts never runs, so judge always returns undefined and the browser coverage check is skipped (its own lines 215-218 uncovered). Excluding evals/ there, the check runs and holds. (Found 22 October, the rendering-under-load work.)

summary: The household test gets other row numbers when run in one process with the wedding's other tests
detail: It passes alone and fails in-process beside them: it relies on ids another test's rows move. (Found 22 October.)

summary: In chat, a new tab's first page waits for a burst of messages to end
detail: Suspected, not verified: chat's presence (inTurn around keepPresence/keepLobby, whoIsWhere going through every socket for each message) puts the open behind each message's keepLobby. The example's code, not the kernel's. (Found 22 October, the rendering-under-load work.)

summary: The page's headers rest on the server fetching its own bundle over its own URL
detail: #117 serves the shell's bundle at an unguessable path and the page's routes fetch it from server.url (Bun gives an HTML bundle no headers of the app's). A server whose url it cannot reach from inside (TLS with a certificate for another name, a bind address that refuses loopback) would fail to serve its page. Fix, when Bun allows: headers on the HTMLBundle route itself; until then a test over TLS. (Found merging #117, 22 October.)

summary: The model's page still reads the word date as a text column
detail: delta now has a date type (#101) and numeric; the modelling vocabulary maps "date" to text, and nothing to numeric. Map date to date, and money or amount words to numeric, where a story says them. (Found 22 October.)
